source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect comprehensive data: Begin by gathering data from continuous emission monitoring systems, periodic stack testing results, and ambient air quality monitoring networks. Document types of pollutants being released, emission rates, and duration of these emissions over both short-term and long-term periods.

3. Establish baseline data.
Compare current emission data with baseline levels established during periods when operations were known to be in compliance. This will help in determining the excess amount being released.

4. Identify the source.
Pinpoint the exact production processes or equipment that are contributing to excessive emissions. Document the operational status (e.g., normal operating conditions, process upsets, or malfunctions) at the time of excessive emissions.

5. Conduct detailed analysis.
Utilize approved methodologies to ensure data accuracy. This might involve using statistical analysis tools or modeling to correlate the emissions with ambient air quality impacts.

6. Document regulatory thresholds.
Refer to local, national, or international regulations (e.g., Clean Air Acts, National
